name: Starter: Sorani Kurdish
about: Sorani word order, joined endings and everyday verbs in real sentences.

words.هەبوون: to exist or have (هەیە: there is; نییە: there isn't)
words.کردن: to do, make (دەکات: does; کار کردن: to work)
words.ڕۆیشتن: to go, to leave (بڕۆم: that I go)
words.کار: work; operation (کار ناکات: it doesn't work)
words.بوون: to be or become (دەبێت: must; ببم: I become)
words.چوون: to go (دەچم: I go; نەچووم: I didn't go)
words.خەڵک: people; a person from a place (خەڵکی کوێ: from where)
words.کڕین: to buy (دەکڕم: I buy; کڕی: bought)
words.بارین: to fall, of rain or snow

slaw-choni.about: The everyday greeting to one person: hello, how are you?

tkaya.about: The everyday polite word placed before or after a request.

glass-water.about: Literally a glass water; Sorani needs no word for of here.

dast-xosh.about: Literally hand well; said to thank someone for work or food.

bbura.about: Literally forgive; used to get attention or apologize to one person.

xwahafiz.about: Literally may God protect you; the ordinary word for goodbye.

items.means: A tea and a water, please.
I have a brother and a sister.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?

items.text: من بە کوردی کەمێک قسە دەکەم.
wrong: من بە کوردی کەمێک قسە دەکەیت.
من بە کوردی کەمێک قسە دەکات.

items.means: Excuse me, where is the train station?
My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I go to the city.
I live in a small house.
The book is on the table.
There isn't anyone in the room.
There's no milk in the fridge.
I'd like a glass of water, please.
Thanks, the bread is really good.
Excuse me, where's the bus stop?
I buy bread at a store.
Does this bus go to Sulaymaniyah?
I didn't go to the market yesterday.
The new shoes are very expensive.
I left my money in the taxi.
Can we see each other tomorrow?

items.text: ئەگەر باران ببارێت، لە ماڵ دەمێنینەوە.
items.means: If it rains, we'll stay home.
wrong: ئەگەر باران ببارێت، لە ماڵ دەدەمێنینەوە.

concept.line: Most present verbs use دە- before the present stem and an ending for the subject: دەکڕم (I buy), دەچیت (you go), دەکەن (they do).
Sorani usually attaches the present copula to the word before it: برسیم (I'm hungry), خەڵکی کوێیت (where are you from?), خۆشە (it is good), کوردین (we are Kurds), گرانن (they are expensive).

words.means: مامۆستام = I am a teacher; مامۆستایت = you are a teacher; مامۆستا = teacher
دایکمە = is my mother; دایکم = my mother
باوکمە = is my father; باوکم = my father

concept.line: A person ending attaches to a noun: ناوم (my name), ناوت (your name), کلیلەکانم (my keys).

words.means: هەیە = there is; نییە = there is not
خوشکێکم = a sister of mine; خوشکم = my sister
کلیلەکە = the key; کلیلەکەم = my key

concept.line: ئایا can introduce a yes-or-no question and has no English word of its own.

words.means: کتێب = book; کتێبم = books of mine
دەکەیت = you do; دەکەم = I do
تێناگەم = I do not understand; تێدەگەیت = you understand
دەوێت = to want (قاوەیەکم دەوێت: I want a coffee)
قاوەیەکم = coffee (قاوەیەکم: a coffee with the clitic -م; in قاوەیەکم دەوێت, 'I want a coffee')
ئاوم = water (ئاوم: my water; in ئاوم دەوێت, 'I want water')

concept.line: The object and other details normally come before the verb: من قاوە ناخۆمەوە (I don't drink coffee); بۆ بازاڕ دەچم (I'm going to the market).

words.means: دەژیم = I live; دەژیت = you live; دەژی = lives
دەڕۆم = I go; دەڕۆیت = you go; دەڕوات = goes
ئۆتۆمبێلێکم = a car of mine; ئۆتۆمبێلە = car

concept.line: The ending -ێک makes a noun indefinite or says one: گڵاسێک (a glass).
